hook: An airliner came down in a lagoon. Navy sailors raced to it.
narration: This airliner had just come down in a lagoon, a quarter mile short of the runway.
Air Niugini flight PX56, at Chuuk, in Micronesia, in September of 2018.
A Navy underwater construction team was working nearby, so they took their inflatable boat straight to it.
By the time they got there, water was already washing over the wing.
A jet in the water floats only as long as air stays trapped inside, so every minute counts.
Sailors climbed onto the sinking wing to reach the people at the doors.
They worked alongside local boats, [short pause] taking people off the wing.
outcome: They got passengers and crew to shore before the jet sank in about one hundred feet of water.
title: Jet crash landed in a Pacific lagoon
description:
Air Niugini flight PX56 crash landed in the lagoon a quarter mile short of the runway at Chuuk, Federated States of Micronesia, on Sept. 28, 2018. Sailors from U.S. Navy Underwater Construction Team 2 used their inflatable boat to help get passengers and crew to shore before the plane sank.

Footage: U.S. Navy video, Underwater Construction Team 2, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/629967/uct-2-renders-assistance-following-plane-crash-chuuk
